description.value: The study investigated spatial orientation in Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia using a virtual supermarket task and structural voxel-based morphometry, including group comparisons and correlations between orientation performance and grey matter integrity.

spans.text: In this study we investigated spatial orientation in 58 dementia patients and 23 healthy controls using a novel virtual supermarket task as well as voxel-based morphometry (VBM).

value: we hypothesized that while orientation is dependent on memory processes, the retrosplenial region would be critical for egocentric spatial orientation, such that spatial orientation would be associated with reduced structural integrity of the RSC.

In the current study, we utilised a virtual supermarket environment that does not require prior learning of a spatial layout to assess spatial orientation in AD and FTD.

description.value: Participants viewed first-person videos of travel through a virtual supermarket and indicated the direction of the starting location at the end of each trial.

spans.text: Participants viewed the environment from a first person perspective and maintained spatial orientation using an egocentric frame of reference.
A total of 14 video trials (2 sections of 7 videos) were created from an English version of the ‘Virtual Supermarket’ ( ) based on Australian and New Zealand supermarkets.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to keep track of the direction of the starting location throughout the videos and decide its direction at the end of each trial.

spans.text: Participants were explicitly told they would start from the same starting location across trials and asked to keep track of the direction of the starting location throughout the videos.

stimuli.value: Videos depicting movement through an English version of a virtual supermarket.
